# Volume 3 — Chapter XXXVII Full-fledged B.A.’s

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

“May I pass away, or let the following evening arrive,” Cressy moaned.
{: #nw-v03-c37-p0000 }

“Provided that your life is sufficiently long, both desires shall be fulfilled,” Nell remarked serenely.
{: #nw-v03-c37-p0001 }

“You can easily remain calm, being comfortable with Philosophy. I am not, and contemplating that dreadful exam tomorrow makes me shudder. What will Ez say if I do not pass?”
{: #nw-v03-c37-p0002 }

“You will not be unsuccessful. In what manner did you fare in Greek today?”
{: #nw-v03-c37-p0003 }

“I am unsure. It might have been a fine composition, or it might have been poor enough that Homer turned in his resting place. My studying and pondering of notebooks have reached a point where I cannot judge anything at all. Little Cressy will feel so grateful once this entire process of examining comes to an end.”
{: #nw-v03-c37-p0004 }

“Examinating? Such a word has never come to my ears.”
{: #nw-v03-c37-p0005 }

“Well, am I not just as entitled to invent a word as anyone else is?” asked Cressy.
{: #nw-v03-c37-p0006 }

“Words are grown rather than made,” remarked Nell.
{: #nw-v03-c37-p0007 }

“Forget about it—I am starting to dimly perceive open sea up ahead where no test waves threaten. Girls, do you—are you able to grasp that our existence at Wexcombe has nearly come to an end?”
{: #nw-v03-c37-p0008 }

“I am unable to,” Nell stated, filled with sorrow. “It feels like only yesterday when Nonie and I found ourselves isolated among all those Freshmen at Wexcombe. And presently we have become Seniors taking our last tests.”
{: #nw-v03-c37-p0009 }

“‘Wise, potent, and reverend Seniors,’” Cressy recited. “Is it your belief that we are truly even a bit wiser than on our arrival at Wexcombe?”
{: #nw-v03-c37-p0010 }

“By times you don’t act like it,” Aunt Euphemia said severely.
{: #nw-v03-c37-p0011 }

“Oh, Aunt Phemie, taking us all in all, haven’t we been fairly good girls during the three winters you’ve acted as a mother to us?” Cressy pleaded.
{: #nw-v03-c37-p0012 }

“The four of you have been the sweetest, dearest, best girls who ever attended college as a group,” declared Aunt Euphemia, who never ruined a flattering remark with uncalled-for thriftiness.
{: #nw-v03-c37-p0013 }

“However, I suspect you still lack a good deal of judgment. Naturally, that is only to be anticipated. Judgment comes from experience. A college education cannot impart it. You have attended college for four years while I never did, yet I possess far greater knowledge than you do, young ladies.”
{: #nw-v03-c37-p0014 }

“‘There is a great deal that fails to adhere to standard rules, A immense amount of wisdom exists That is completely unattainable at university, A vast quantity of information remains untaught in the classroom,’”
{: #nw-v03-c37-p0015 }

cited Mabel.
{: #nw-v03-c37-p0016 }

“Was there anything you acquired at Wexcombe besides geometry, dead languages, and similar rubbish?” asked Aunt Euphemia.
{: #nw-v03-c37-p0017 }

“Oh, indeed. My belief is that we have done so, Aunty,” Nell objected.
{: #nw-v03-c37-p0018 }

“What Professor Woodleigh shared with us this past Philomathic has now been proven true to us,” Cressy remarked. “The statement he made was, ‘In the banquet of life, humor serves as the most zesty seasoning. Let your errors amuse you while teaching you, find amusement in your hardships while drawing power from them, and turn your obstacles into a laughing matter while mastering them.’ Is that not a lesson of value, Aunt Phemie?”
{: #nw-v03-c37-p0019 }

“Indeed, it is, my dear. If you have acquired the ability to smile at matters deserving of laughter, while refraining from laughing at those that do not, you possess both wisdom and comprehension.”
{: #nw-v03-c37-p0020 }

“Nell, what did you gain from the course you took at Wexcombe?” Honora softly asked off to the side.
{: #nw-v03-c37-p0021 }

“It is my belief,” Nell uttered deliberately, “that I have truly come to regard every minor obstacle as a joke and every major one as a sign of impending triumph. Taking everything into account, I believe that is the gift Wexcombe has bestowed upon me.”
{: #nw-v03-c37-p0022 }

“Expressing what it has accomplished for me requires me to rely once more on a quote from Professor Woodleigh,” Honora stated. “Do you recall him saying during his speech, ‘If we but possess the vision to perceive it, the soul to cherish it, and the reach to claim it for our own, the world offers us so very much—an abundance within mankind, an abundance within creative works and writings, an abundance in every place to bring joy and inspire gratitude.’ Nell, I believe that Wexcombe has imparted that lesson to me to a certain degree.”
{: #nw-v03-c37-p0023 }

“Based on what everyone is saying,” Aunt Euphemia observed, “it boils down to the fact that four years of college can impart to you—provided you possess sufficient innate common sense—the same knowledge that roughly twenty years of life experience would take to instill. Well, as far as I am concerned, that validates higher education. Prior to this, I had always held doubts regarding the issue.”
{: #nw-v03-c37-p0024 }

“Aunt Phemie, what about the folks who lack natural gumption, though?”
{: #nw-v03-c37-p0025 }

“Individuals devoid of innate common sense never acquire it,” Aunt Euphemia shot back, “whether in university or throughout existence. Should they survive until a century old, their actual knowledge remains no greater than it was at birth. It is a calamity for them, not a failing, wretched creatures. Nevertheless, those among us blessed with a degree of common sense ought to properly express gratitude to the Almighty for it.”
{: #nw-v03-c37-p0026 }

“Aunt Phemie, would you mind explaining the meaning of gumption?” Cressy inquired.
{: #nw-v03-c37-p0027 }

“No, I will not, young woman. Whoever possesses gumption understands its meaning, while whoever lacks it will remain perpetually ignorant of its meaning. Consequently, defining it serves no purpose.”
{: #nw-v03-c37-p0028 }

The packed days passed quickly, and tests reached their conclusion. Nell earned High Honors in English. Honora earned Honors in Classics, whereas Cressy did so in Mathematics. Mabel achieved a respectable overall performance. Subsequently, Convocation took place.
{: #nw-v03-c37-p0029 }

“This is what I would once have called an epoch in my life,” Nell remarked while removing Cyril’s violets from their box and contemplating them deeply. Intending to wear them, naturally, she nevertheless let her gaze drift toward a second box sitting on her table. Filled to the brim with lilies-of-the-valley, they were just as fresh and sweetly scented as the ones that blossomed in the yard at Grey Shutters whenever June arrived in Brierley. Adjacent to the box rested Hugh Carrow’s card.
{: #nw-v03-c37-p0030 }

Nell pondered the reason Hugh had gifted her flowers for Convocation. Throughout the previous winter, she had encountered him on very few occasions. Since the Christmas holidays, his visits to Tabby’s Place amounted to just a single Friday evening, and their encounters in other locations were infrequent. It was clear to her that his intense focus on his studies was aimed at achieving High Honors and the Cooper Prize, leaving him minimal involvement in Wexcombe's social activities. In contrast, Nell’s own winter had contained a great deal of social entertainment. Her interactions with the Gardners had been frequent; her bond with Dorothy was extremely close; and within college circles, the news of her engagement to Cyril was anticipated at any moment. Nell was anticipating it as well. Nevertheless, right before departing Tabby’s Place to attend Convocation, she discarded Cyril’s violets and substituted Hugh’s lilies-of-the-valley. The motive behind her action was something she was unable to explain. For some reason, as her long-held ambitions were being realized, past Brierley times, aspirations, and companionships felt remarkably near. In former times, she and Hugh had playfully imagined the occasion when they would both be graduates in Arts, wearing caps and gowns. That extraordinary day had finally arrived, and Cyril’s violets did not fit into it. Only the blossoms from her long-standing friend appeared to suit this realization of early-blooming dreams that he had formerly shared.
{: #nw-v03-c37-p0031 }

This date had enticed and charmed her for years; yet when it arrived, the sole, sharp, lasting recollection it imparted to her was not the gasp-inducing instant in which the dignified president of Wexcombe presented her diploma and cap while greeting her as a B.A.; nor was it the sparkle in Hugh’s eyes upon noticing her lilies, or the bewildered, hurt look Cyril cast toward her while passing her on the platform. It was not Aline Lisle’s patronizing felicitations, nor Dorothy’s passionate, spontaneous expressions of goodwill. It was a single peculiar, inexplicable ache that ruined this long-anticipated date for her, leaving within it a specific subtle yet lasting trace of resentment.
{: #nw-v03-c37-p0032 }

The graduates in Arts hosted a dance for their graduation that evening. As Nell got ready for the event, she set aside the pearl beads that she normally put on and removed from her trunk the little box delivered to Grey Shutters on Christmas day. A gold chain as thin as a thread, featuring a tiny pink heart in enamel for a pendant, was inside it. The card included with it bore the inscription, “With all good wishes from your old chum, Hugh.” Nell—who had laughed at the recollection the enamel heart brought to mind of that disastrous day when Hugh dubbed her “Carrots” and unsuccessfully attempted to reconcile using a pink sugar heart—had sent him a pleasant, brief message of gratitude. However, she had yet to wear the piece of jewelry. On this night, displaying a dreamy smile, she secured it around her fair neck.
{: #nw-v03-c37-p0033 }

Together, she and Cressy made their way on foot to Wexcombe. While Nell proceeded without speaking, Cressy prattled about various topics. Unexpectedly, she remarked,
{: #nw-v03-c37-p0034 }

“I was told today that the news of Hugh Carrow’s betrothal to Rowena Calder would be made public right after Convocation ended. Have you heard anything about that?”
{: #nw-v03-c37-p0035 }

“No,” Nell said.
{: #nw-v03-c37-p0036 }

“I believe that is accurate,” Cressy remarked in a light tone.
{: #nw-v03-c37-p0037 }

Nell kept silent. She could feel her face glowing hot within the dark. Sliding her hand beneath her collar, she grasped the chain made of gold. It snapped after a single forceful twist. Nell jammed the fractured piece of jewelry into her pocket. Her eyes stung while her hands shook.
{: #nw-v03-c37-p0038 }

Yet among the joyous partygoers that evening, her mirth surpassed everyone else's, and she expressed no regret when informing Hugh that no dances remained on her card when he approached to request one. Later on, while joining the girls by the fading fire at Tabby’s Place to warm their satin skins against the chill of spring, her talk about the day's happenings was as cheerful as anyone's.
{: #nw-v03-c37-p0039 }

“Elias Purdy MacKinnon came by this evening following your departure,” remarked Aunt Euphemia, having remained awake to maintain the fire. “The commencement dance was news to him. That young man should wear an elastic strip around his skull at night so his ears learn to lie flat. A former suitor of mine used one, which benefited his appearance tremendously. Because I was the person who recommended the idea to him, he followed my counsel, yet he held it against me for the rest of his days.”
{: #nw-v03-c37-p0040 }

“Elias Purdy is an exceptionally solemn young man,” Honora remarked with a yawn. “He occupies himself with more weighty issues than his ears. You are aware he intends to become a minister.”
{: #nw-v03-c37-p0041 }

“Well, I suppose the Lord doesn’t regard the ears of a man,” Aunt Euphemia remarked solemnly, ceasing any additional disapproval of Elias Purdy. Aunt Euphemia maintained a suitable deference toward the clergy, even when it concerned an unseasoned preacher.
{: #nw-v03-c37-p0042 }
